features.details: Ghostty-accurate VT handling, true color, minimum text contrast of 3 by default (Ghostty `minimum-contrast` from 1 to 21; 1 disables adjustment), readable text even when a running agent retains its prompt background across a theme change, wide glyphs, IME input, mouse selection and reporting, scrollback search (`cmd-f`), cmd-click links and file paths, including space-containing paths in parentheses, also after a note such as `(see …)`, across soft-wrapped rows, right-click actions on paths (reveal in Finder, open a tab or `cd` there, copy), drag and drop paths, inline images (Kitty graphics protocol), Mermaid diagrams in agent output rendered offline ("View diagram"), Markdown files previewed in the browser (right-click a `.md` path, or "Preview Markdown" in the palette), font size shortcuts, prompt jumping (`cmd-up` / `cmd-down`) Right-click a terminal selection for Copy for sharing: review and edit a plain-text preview before copying. It uses only uniquely matched assistant text from the selected pane’s exact conversation; partial selections stay partial and ambiguous selections remain unchanged. Confirmed Claude Code 2.1.294 and Codex 0.161.0 answer gutters are removed only when the entire selected answer matches its original text. Ordinary Copy keeps the existing terminal selection behavior. Changed conversations block copying; cancelling restores typing focus.
features.title: Ghostty inside
features.summary: True color, Unicode, IME, search, your Ghostty font and colors, and readable prompt text across theme changes. Follow links and space-containing paths across wrapped rows, show Kitty graphics, and preview Mermaid diagrams and Markdown offline. Review and edit selected agent text before copying it for sharing.

features.details: Open another window with cmd-shift-n. Windows, terminal, Git tree and Diff review tabs, splits, active focus, directories and exact supported agent conversations come back after restart. Previous working activity remains available separately from new runtime output. Every tab has a visible close button, including long labels and inactive tabs; cmd-w closes the focused pane. Working or waiting agents ask before stopping.
features.title: Keep your place, close safely
features.summary: Restore windows, layouts and supported agent conversations. Keep previous working context and close one pane or a whole tab safely.

features.details: In a configured, signed macOS release, click Update to download, verify and install with Sparkle. Progress is shared across windows; installation waits for current repository tasks and unfinished input before preserving sessions. macOS asks for administrator approval when required. Windows briefly reopen while running shells and agents, terminal text and scrollback, pane IDs, layouts and focus reconnect. Failed installation or startup reopens the retained signed app with the same sessions. Terminals that have used inline images block the update without stopping their processes. Release notes and version dismissal remain separate; automatic downloads and installs are off. v0.1.19 requires one manual update first.
features.title: Update without stopping your work
features.summary: Click Update in the signed macOS app. Running shells and agents reconnect with their text, scrollback and window layouts. Installation failure reopens the retained app with your sessions; inline-image terminals ask you to close them first.

features.details: The focused pane's repository and branch-note alias appear as repo - task; the branch is the fallback. Custom tab names remain on tabs without hiding the repository context. Hover for the repository, full note, branch and worktree path. Open the focused worktree in a chosen installed editor or Finder.
features.title: The task in the title
features.summary: See the repository and focused branch task together. Hover for the full context or open the worktree in your favorite editor.

features.title: Keep operational messages in view
features.summary: Open the title-bar bell icon for timestamped messages, unread arrivals and exact agent-pane links. Closing the list returns typing focus without deleting history.
features.details: The title-bar notification control stays immediately before the installed-app picker, even with the sidebar hidden or no available picker. Window-local history lists severity, date and UTC time, message and known directory/tab/pane context newest first. Opening reads only existing arrivals; later arrivals remain unread. Selecting an agent event goes to its exact still-open pane. Operational errors and successes no longer overwrite a single sidebar message; an ongoing branch update changes one entry. OS notifications and provider usage controls remain available. History retains at most 500 entries and reports removed older entries. Normal restart clears it; session-preserving updates retain each window's history and read state.

Repositories and plain folders, worktrees, dirty / ahead / behind / conflict badges, lines added and removed against the default branch (click for a read-only diff tab), pull request state via `gh`, `glab` or `tea`, and open-tab counts. Two peer sections, Sessions and PROJECT, each have a header outside their own scrolling list; the wheel or trackpad moves only the list under the pointer. Sessions has one row per agent pane, so agents in split panes each get a row, numbered when they share a tab; one row per Git tree or diff review tab; and ordinary terminal tabs last, all in tab and pane order. Rows never move when an agent starts working, waits, finishes or goes idle, and a live idle agent is listed once. Each row shows its repository and branch, or the branch note with the Alias / Branch toggle, what it is, time since the last terminal activity and a status icon whose tooltip names the state: Working, Waiting for input, Turn complete, Idle, No live agent, Terminal, Git tree or Diff review. Close an ordinary terminal tab or a live idle agent's pane directly from its row; the usual close confirmation applies. Sessions grows with its rows up to 40% of the sidebar and then scrolls, takes the remaining height when PROJECT is collapsed and shows No open sessions when empty. Clicking a session, switching tabs or panes and jumping to an agent focus the exact pane and highlight its branch in PROJECT, which scrolls only enough to reveal a clipped worktree while keeping its repository name visible. Sessions never scrolls by itself, and a collapsed PROJECT section stays collapsed with the highlight updated. Explicit PROJECT navigation, such as a worktree or its status dot, STARRED, Go to worktree or a notification whose pane is gone, expands PROJECT when needed. Background output, status changes and refreshes move neither list. Both sections collapse independently, show their counts while collapsed and remember the choice across restarts; earlier ACTIVE and IDLE settings carry over as a collapsed Sessions only when both were collapsed. Every badge explains itself on hover. Repositories and folders, including STARRED branches, sit beneath PROJECT; use the individual repository disclosures. Drag a repository header above or below another to reorder the list; a line marks where it lands, PROJECT scrolls near its edges, and the order is saved without moving folders or changing Git. Right-click a branch and choose "Add to Starred" to keep it in a STARRED list within PROJECT, per repository and saved across restarts; click a starred row to go to its worktree, or its star to unstar it without leaving the current tab. Selecting a worktree reuses its most recently focused pane across windows. If the system cannot open the folder picker for Add repository, chda keeps running with terminals, typed input and settings unchanged, records one error in the title-bar notifications, and you can try again or drop the folder on the sidebar. A working agent shows a spinning ring, an agent waiting for input an orange "!" badge on a tinted row, a finished turn a green dot, a live idle agent a yellow dot and a row with no live agent a gray dot.
features.title: Live sessions at a glance
features.summary: Browse Sessions and PROJECT side by side, each scrolling on its own. Clicking a session never moves the list; PROJECT highlights its branch and reveals it with minimal scrolling. Close ordinary terminals and idle agents directly and read GitHub PR state colors independently of checks.

features.details: Create from a new or existing branch, delete with a safety check, merge-and-clean, bulk cleanup of merged branches, update a branch from its upstream when it is clean and no agent works in it (fast-forward; a diverged branch asks before a rebase or merge and never rewrites pushed commits); a note per branch saying what the task is (right-click "Edit note...", or `chda note <text>` inside the worktree), shown as the row's label and searchable in the palette Creation and note forms share labeled fields, a multiline note area, readable destination/context, explicit Cancel/Create/Save buttons and busy/error feedback. Cmd-V and Edit > Paste insert at the caret or replace selected text, including Unicode notes; single-line branch input flattens line breaks without submitting. Worktree preparation in the repository menu starts with empty command and file lists. Save ordered commands and explicit relative paths without executing them. First or changed plans show the actual new working directory, source/destination paths and steps for confirmation; imported settings never grant permission. Only untracked gitignored regular files are copied, through directory handles that reject symlinks and path traversal. Copies are independent and never overwrite existing files. Setup runs off the UI thread in the configured shell, after copying, with stage and exit feedback. Cancel stops owned preparation processes; failures keep the worktree and copied files. Review retry keeps existing regular files and reruns commands from the beginning, or explicitly Skip. Successful background preparation leaves tabs and typing focus alone; Open starts the planned terminal or the existing per-launch agent options. Setup in the title bar reopens hidden runs. Other windows and MCP requests cannot bypass outstanding preparation. Unfinished runs and editors defer session-preserving updates.
features.title: One worktree per task
features.summary: Create from any branch, label it with a note, read its diff, update from upstream, then merge and clean up with checks for unsaved or unpushed work. Opt in to selected local-file copies and ordered setup commands before opening a new worktree.

features.details: Right-click a repository and choose "View Git tree" for a read-only commit graph with parent connections, subjects, short hashes and local / remote branches, tags and HEAD. History loads in pages as you scroll; refresh or retry without opening a shell. One graph tab per repository; graph tabs restore after a restart.
features.title: Read the Git tree
features.summary: Choose View Git tree from the repository menu for commit connections, subjects, short hashes and branch, tag and HEAD labels. Browse in a read-only tab, refresh and restore it after restarting.

features.title: Review changes with private notes
features.summary: Choose Review diff from a worktree menu. Select old or new lines, add private notes and preview a batch for an exact live agent conversation. Copy and focus its pane, then paste when ready.
features.details: One native review tab per worktree keeps the existing diff pager available. Browse a unified diff with old/new line numbers and a file list that collapses in narrow windows; Shift-click selects a range within one hunk. Add, edit and resolve local notes. Exact unchanged context reconnects after refresh; missing or ambiguous locations stay Stale and require explicit reattachment. Renames keep both path identities; binary and metadata-only changes have no text anchors. Notes persist privately across restarts; failed saves keep editable drafts. Send review notes previews selected notes against a freshly read diff, including original locations for stale notes. Choose an exact live provider/conversation in the same Git worktree. Copy and go to agent rechecks the diff, notes and target, copies plain text and focuses its pane. Paste manually; direct delivery is unavailable. Working and approval-waiting input is never cleared, pasted into or automatically submitted. Copying does not resolve notes or claim delivery; changed conversations block the copy. Open editors and previews defer session-preserving updates.

Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI and OpenCode status from their own hooks on tabs, the Sessions list, worktree rows and the Dock badge; notifications that open the agent's pane; jump to the agent that waits (`cmd-shift-a`); session list ordered by the last message, with token usage and one-click resume; cmd-click several sessions to resume them side by side in one tab; managed Claude Code and Codex launches show Use CLI configuration (the default) or explicit Bypass before starting, including presets, selected conversations and worktree default actions. Codex Bypass disables approvals and sandboxing. Conflicting preset permission options stop the launch without rewriting the preset. Captured executable, working directory, options and permission choice follow the exact conversation on resume and restore; inherited effective policy is shown as unobserved. When a chda-launched agent exits, its pane shows the exit state and retains the last run as read-only Previous run output. Restart uses the same pane, recorded directory, executable, options, permission choice and exact verified conversation; repeated clicks start one successor. Missing executable, directory or transcript produces an error instead of a fresh conversation. A provider without verifiable local transcripts explains that exact resume is unavailable. Live turn completion and commands typed directly in a surviving shell do not offer restart. Stopped panes and previous output survive cold restart and session-preserving updates; available account reports are retained as reports, with CLI authentication inherited. Expand provider-confirmed Claude and Codex children below their exact parent agent row in Sessions, where they stay when the parent becomes idle. Rows show working, waiting, turn complete, ended or unknown reports, with stable ordering and independent disclosure. A child opens only its exact known dedicated pane; otherwise it shows status details. Claude child hooks omit prompts and answers; Codex queries the existing local CLI daemon through its WebSocket byte proxy with exact parent IDs and metadata only. Unavailable or unloaded runtime state remains unknown, and older CLIs retain their existing top-level behavior. Children do not add usage a second time. Cold restart clears child activity; session-preserving updates retain reports and disclosure state.
features.title: Agents you can see
features.summary: Track Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI and OpenCode. Notifications open the right pane; past conversations resume together or side by side. Choose per-launch permissions for Claude Code and Codex; retain captured options when reopening a conversation. Keep an exited agent’s output and restart its exact known conversation in the same pane. Expand confirmed child activity under its parent; inspect state without jumping to a different conversation.

features.title: Quota and local session resources
features.summary: See Claude Code and Codex quota, clear loading and retry states, reset countdowns, and selected-pane CPU, memory and listeners. Open bottom-left details with labeled bars for each reported quota window.
features.details: The bottom bar reports provider quota, never inferred from token counts. Startup shows Waiting for usage for Claude Code and Loading for Codex. Empty reports preserve the same session or account's last valid reading and its actual age. All windows share reports and one Codex query loop; transient failures retry promptly, and a verified account's retained reading is labeled retrying. Authentication and installation problems have specific labels and details. Claude Code reports through a per-launch status line; Codex uses the local app-server account protocol. Details separate accounts or unknown session scopes and quota windows. On macOS, selected-pane PTY descendants supply CPU, summed RSS, listening endpoints, process count and uptime. Sampling runs off the UI thread with deadlines. See docs/status-bar.md for scopes and refresh behavior. Click either provider to open details above the bottom-left controls. Each reported quota window has a labeled 0–100% bar, value and reset time; scope, source, observed age, historical reports and errors stay distinct. Unknown data creates no bar. Content scrolls inside the window.
`cmd-shift-p`: every action, worktree, agent launch and session in one fuzzy list
features.title: Every action in one place
features.summary: Press `cmd-shift-p` to find worktrees, launch agents, resume sessions and run actions. Agents can create worktrees and open tabs through `chda mcp`.

features.details: Reads your Ghostty font, colors and padding; chda's own settings in one TOML file; edits apply without a restart; executable discovery uses the login-shell PATH, with a validated ~/.local/bin/claude fallback for native Claude Code installations
features.title: Your terminal, your settings
features.summary: Reuse your Ghostty font, colors and padding. Edit chda's TOML settings without restarting. Homebrew and version-manager agents are found through your login shell's PATH.
